thesis: Penguin Solutions is the small-cap sleeper of this watchlist: record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $478.7M (+48% y/y, big beat), AI-driven businesses now 74% of sales growing 104% y/y, backlog building, and FY2026 guidance raised hard (net sales +22% and non-GAAP EPS ~$2.60, up from +12% and $2.15) with management framing ~30% growth again in FY2027. At ~$3.1B (~26x FY26 EPS, ~20x the FY27 frame) it is the only richly-growing name on the list not trading at bubble multiples - though margin mix (gross margin -3.6pp y/y), the Penguin Edge wind-down, and the transition away from hyperscale customer Meta are live drags.
catalysts: Q4 FY2026 results (~October 2026) against raised guidance (+22% sales, ~$2.60 EPS)
FY2027 outlook formalization: management contemplates ~30% growth in sales and EPS
Non-hyperscale AI infrastructure demand outpacing reported sales - growing backlog converts
Integrated memory attach to AI systems (74% of sales, +104% y/y momentum)
Analyst target catch-up: the stock trades above street targets (Rosenblatt raised to $75)
risk_factors: Customer/segment transition: Advanced Computing declining 15-20% for the year on the Penguin Edge wind-down and the move away from Meta as a hyperscale customer
Margin mix: non-GAAP gross margin down 3.6pp y/y; the AI-infrastructure mix is lower-margin than legacy
Competitive: Dell, Supermicro, HPE and white-box vendors all chase the same non-hyperscale AI infrastructure budgets
Small-cap volatility: beta 2.83; same-day quote conflicts this week (-10.67% and +10.15% prints across sources) show a thin, fast tape
Memory-price exposure: integrated-memory economics ride the same DRAM cycle that will eventually turn
